hero.title:
Understand.
Question. Act.
hero.intro: I want a democracy in which everyone can understand, propose, decide and hold power accountable. Here I share resources that reflect my concerns: popular sovereignty, equality, justice and transparency.
hero.invitation: An invitation to explore and make up your own mind.
hero.signature: A personal selection, open to disagreement.
hero.context: Find the text behind a vote, compare arguments, understand who owns a media outlet or discover ways to participate: these tools offer practical starting points. From there, everyone can cross-check sources and take their thinking further.

featured.title: Four starting points.
featured.intro: Different approaches, a shared purpose: understanding more and taking part in democratic life. These resources focus on France.

scene.hint: Scroll to discover the next resource

more.title: A question. A path to explore.
more.intro: A document to find, an argument to examine, a vote to check: a few paths to explore further.

projects.title: What I’m building, too.
projects.intro: These initiatives inform my own projects. Two complementary ways to make debate and power easier to examine.

agora.name: Agora
agora.label: A graph of debates
agora.description: Connect arguments, objections, facts and sources to understand where a disagreement lies, without imposing a conclusion.
agora.intention: The intention: trace a conclusion back to its supporting arguments and sources, while keeping objections visible.

observatory.name: The Observatory
observatory.label: Power and transparency
observatory.description: Make the exercise of power understandable and verifiable: representatives, votes, interests and civic action.
observatory.details: A future direction: exploring media ownership
observatory.future: An interactive map to search for a media outlet, follow its ownership links and examine sources. This module remains a planned extension with the Observatory; it is not yet available here.
observatory.intention: The intention: start with a concrete question, find the documents and understand what they actually establish.

approach.title:
A point of view.
Room for yours.
approach.body: This selection is personal and reflects my commitments. Equality between women and men, the distribution of wealth, direct democracy — including citizen-initiated referendums — and media independence are among the questions that matter to me.
approach.humility: My convictions and analyses can change. Sharing a resource does not mean endorsing every position it takes. You do not need to share mine to find useful information or arguments to discuss here.

principles.title: Visible credits
principles.body: Each initiative is attributed to its team. Links take you directly to the original resources.

principles.title: Explicit limitations
principles.body: Facts can be checked against sources; analyses offer an interpretation; convictions express choices. Each card offers context without treating these three as interchangeable.

principles.title: A selection to revisit
principles.body: Links and descriptions are checked periodically. The date is not a certification or a full audit of the service.

approach.contact: Found a broken link or something to clarify?
approach.privacy: The referenced websites are not embedded in this page. You visit them by following their links.
approach.intent: I want to open doors rather than prescribe a single path. Taking time to read a source, understand its context and consider objections is part of this approach too. These tools can inform our conversations and initiatives; they cannot replace debate or our collective choices.

leurs-votes.description: Explore votes in the French National Assembly by topic and compare political groups’ positions. A starting point for looking at actions beyond statements.
leurs-votes.limit: Distinguish recorded votes from the editorial selection and interpretation of topics.
leurs-votes.method: The project is run by Bon Pote. Returning to the ballot and the underlying text helps put a thematic presentation in context.

monvote2027.description: Compare your answers with positions attributed to political figures, then examine sources and disagreements topic by topic.
monvote2027.limit: Scores depend on the questions and their weighting. They are not enough to decide how to vote.
monvote2027.method: The team describes itself as anonymous volunteers. Its methodology explains the calculation and its limits: simplified positions, changing programmes and no assessment of past performance or credibility.

praxis.owner: The Praxis team, initiated by François Boulo
praxis.description: Read analyses and explore consultations on concrete proposals. A connection between information and participation.
praxis.limit: Self-selected participants do not necessarily represent the population. These consultations are not official binding referendums.
praxis.method: Praxis presents a media and civic participation project. Access depends on the content and features. Its citizen-initiated referendum module is listed as a future development; an announcement does not establish availability.

transparence.description: Explore public document requests, publications and actions to make the exercise of power and the use of public money more transparent.
transparence.limit: A report or ongoing proceeding is not a court ruling establishing the alleged facts.
transparence.method: The association publishes its actions and documents obtained. For each case, distinguish the original document, the association’s interpretation and the status of any proceedings.

madada.description: Browse requests already sent to public authorities and prepare a request for a public document, such as expenses, a grant or a contract.
madada.limit: Exchanges are generally public. Some documents cannot be disclosed: read the conditions before sharing personal information.
madada.method: MaDada supports access to administrative documents in France. Reading an existing request is a useful first step; requesting a document does not itself trigger an investigation.
madada.question: How can I access a public document?
madada.teaser: Find an existing request or prepare your own request to a public body.

wikidebats.owner: Le Laboratoire du débat méthodique and contributors
wikidebats.description: Examine arguments for and against a proposition, follow objections and return to sources to form your own opinion.
wikidebats.limit: The presence or number of arguments does not establish their strength. Examine their sources and possible responses.
wikidebats.method: This collaborative encyclopaedia publishes its content under CC BY-SA 4.0. This page links to the original and does not reproduce its debate collections.
wikidebats.question: What about the opposing arguments?
wikidebats.teaser: Explore arguments, objections and their sources around the same question.

datan.description: Go deeper into MPs’ votes and parliamentary indicators after an initial introduction to a topic or ballot.
datan.limit: Check the period and indicator definitions. Voting records do not capture all parliamentary work.
datan.method: Datan explains its statistics and introduces its team and scientific council. Its methods help clarify what each comparison measures.
datan.question: How did my representative vote?
datan.teaser: Look at voting records and indicators to examine what your representatives do.

medias.name: French media: who owns what?
medias.owner: Acrimed and Le Monde diplomatique · Jérémie Fabre and Marie Beyer
medias.description: Identify major ownership links in French media. A documentary resource for understanding the organisations behind the news.
medias.limit: The map is selective and dated. Ownership alone does not establish the content of an article.
medias.method: The Acrimed page is dated 21 January 2026. The data repository states December 2024 and an ODC-By licence; those dates do not establish that the map and data are synchronised.
medias.question: Who owns the media I read?
medias.teaser: Find a media outlet within the main ownership links in the French press.
